Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
On Wed, 24 Nov 1999 corr...@my-deja.com wrote:

> Hi everyone,
>
> I have a few question, 1ªWhat happen if I block a minion with Kallista
> and play Eagles Eyes in superior version (the text says " this vampire
> attempt to block any action of any minion" )to Selma, and she play E.I
> in superior version, could my vampire block this action.

Eagle's Sight only allows you to break the rules on who normally gets to
block an action e.g. If Methuselah A rushes a vampire of Methuselah B, I,
being Methuselah C, don't normally get a chance to block. Playing Eagle's
Sight allows me to. If, for some reason, my vampire is unable to block,
they are still unable to block. Eagle's Sight simply allows them to
attempt it - it does not break through other cards to allow you to block,
say, an unblockable action.

> 2ª Can play master discipline to a vampire in torpor in my region??

Yes. (I think.)

--

James Coupe

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
corr...@my-deja.com wrote:

> In article <81hshp$ivm$1...@nnrp1.deja.com>,
> corr...@my-deja.com wrote:
> > Hi everyone,
> >
> > I have a few question, 1ªWhat happen if I block a minion with Kallista
> > and play Eagles Eyes in superior version (the text says " this vampire
> > attempt to block any action of any minion" )to Selma, and she play E.I
> > in superior version, could my vampire block this action.

That's Eagle's Sight, not Eagles Eyes.
And no, she cannot attempt to block again.
Eagle's Sight only allows a minion to circumvent the regular rules of
"who may block" - minions controlled by the target in the case of directed
actions and minions controlled by the prey and predator of the acting
minion in the case of a undirected action. [RTR 13-APR-1995]

> > 2ª Can play master discipline to a vampire in torpor in my region??

Yes.

> 3ªCan a vampire gain blood via H.Ground or Giant Blood?? I think that
> yes.

?
Yes, by card text.
A torpored vampire cannot gain blood by H.Ground (card text).
And uncontrolled vampires cannot gain blood by either effect.
